summary: The note describes a resurgence of interest in coastal gastronomy built around seafood and seaweed, tied to sustainability and local economic renewal. It follows events from September 2023 to April 2024, including Chef Annabelle Wright's restaurant, the Coastal Harvest Program, expert commentary on economics and nutrition, a food festival, and school programs. Its main themes are sustainability, economic development, and culinary innovation.
one_line: Coastal communities revive seafood and seaweed cuisine through sustainable fishing, innovative chefs, festivals, and education, linking tradition, health, and economic development.
key_facts: Chef Annabelle Wright's restaurant, Neptune's Bounty, opened on September 15, 2023.
The Coastal Harvest Program launched on October 1, 2023, to boost regional development while ensuring ecological balance, with participating farmers and fishermen committing to responsible practices.

An economic analysis in late November 2023 highlighted the impact of sustainable practices; economist Dr. Lena Richards called sustainable fishing 'an intelligent economic strategy' that creates jobs and sustains local businesses.
Local seaweed varieties such as laver and dulse are making their way into international markets.
On December 12, 2023, nutritionist Hannah Peterson called seaweed a 'superfood that's been hiding in plain sight' at a health and wellness conference, citing thyroid support and plant-based Omega-3.
A trend toward 'aquatic cuisine' began in foodie circles as 2024 dawned, emphasizing the culinary possibilities of the ocean.

Chef Wright's signature dish 'Mermaid's Whisper' combines seasonal catch from scallops to sea bass with various seaweeds; critic Oliver Hammond called it an 'ode to the sea' in his January 2024 review.
The Sea & Seaweed Festival on February 20, 2024, introduced thousands to marine gastronomy with cooking demonstrations, taste-testing, and seaweed foraging excursions.
Captain Stanley Morris, a third-generation fisherman, said in a March 3, 2024 interview that they follow the seasons, respect breeding cycles, and 'only take what we need.'
Starting April 2024, students in coastal regions will learn marine biology, sustainable fishing, and culinary arts as part of regular school curriculums.
Educator Julia Torres said the school program is about understanding ecosystems and fostering a generation that will innovate on culinary heritage.
A resurgence of interest in local gastronomy began in September 2023, spearheaded by culinary figures like Chef Wright.
